newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.5 percent in February.
newsitem.headline: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.5 percent in February.

text.p: Canada's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, rose 0.5 percent in February after rising 0.6 percent in January, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday.
Note: GDP figures are in billions of dollars, seasonally adjusted at annual rates at factor cost, constant 1986 dollars.

Statistics Canada said growth in February picked up in construction and remained firm in several groups of industries. Construction activity rose 3.1 percent in the month, led by a 7.8 percent jump in residential construction.
Manufacturers, wholeslaers and retailers also enjoyed a good month, as they did in January, the federal agency said.

The agency said communication services as well as community, business and personal services continued to increase while rebounds in the mining sector as well as transportation and storage services added to the overall gain.
Declines in the output of utilities, financial and related services and public administration restrained growth, StatsCan said.
(For more information from Statistics Canada contact Michel Girard, Industry Measures and Analysis Division, at 613-951-9145).
